To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Multimorbidity (co-occurrence of 2 or more chronic conditions, functional impairments, or geriatric conditions) is associated with worse prospective health status, more major health decline, higher mortality risk, and more health care utilization.
the prospective effects of baseline multimorbity on health outcomes (fair or poor health status and major health decline) and mortality were significant.

multimorbidity, defined as the co-occurrence or combination of chronic conditions, geriatric syndromess and functional limitations, was associated with worse health outcomes, including poor health status, increased risk of major health decline, increased risk of mortality, and increased health care costs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of chronic conditions on health outcomes in the elderly.
the impact of multimorbidity (co-occurring chronic conditions) on health outcomes.
the prospective effects of co-occurring chronic conditions on health outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study shows the cumulative effects of co-occurring chronic conditions, functional impairments, and geriatric symptoms on the outcomes of poor self-rated health, major health decline and mortality.
“multimorbidity is associated with worse health outcomes, but it is not clear if multimorbidity is a cause or effect.”
multimorbidity is associated with poor health status, a high likelihood of major health decline and increased mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multimorbidity is a powerful predictor of adverse health outcomes in middle-aged and older populations.
multimorbidity is associated with poor health outcomes and that this is true even for those who do not have a single condition that is severe enough to be considered a chronic disease.
the more chronic conditions an older adult has, the worse the health status, the higher the risk of a major health decline, or the more likely the person will die within 2 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multimorbidity is associated with poor health outcomes.
the more conditions an older adult has, the more likely the adult will have adverse health outcomes.
multimorbidity is a powerful predictor of adverse outcomes, and it should be used in research and in practice to identify those who are most in need of care and support.
